annotations.betterLine: Play Flooded Strand instead of Swamp. This keeps Revolt available for Fatal Push on the opponent's turn, which is critical for dealing with threats. The 1 life cost is worth the tactical flexibility, especially at 11 life.

annotations.description: Casting Seasoned Pyromancer before playing Mountain forces exerting Arena of Glory to generate {R}{R}, meaning Arena won't untap next turn. Playing Mountain first provides the third red source, allowing Seasoned Pyromancer to be cast with Mountain + Sacred Foundry + Plains without needing to exert Arena of Glory.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Seasoned Pyromancer before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first, then cast Seasoned Pyromancer using Mountain ({R}) + Sacred Foundry ({R}) + Plains ({1}) without needing to exert Arena of Glory, preserving it for future turns.

annotations.description: Cast a second Fatal Push targeting Ocelot Pride when there was already a Fatal Push on the stack targeting the same creature. The first Fatal Push alone would destroy the 1-mana Ocelot Pride, making the second copy completely wasted. This throws away a premium removal spell for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a second Fatal Push targeting Ocelot Pride while the first Fatal Push was already on the stack targeting it.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and let the first Fatal Push resolve to destroy Ocelot Pride, saving the second Fatal Push in hand for a future threat like Seasoned Pyromancer or another creature.

annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Flooded Strand is slightly suboptimal. Flooded Strand provides deck thinning and, more importantly, can enable Revolt for Fatal Push (relevant if drawn later or in future turns). Additionally, fetching with Flooded Strand puts a land in the graveyard, which helps fuel Phlage's escape cost if the player ever needs to use graveyard resources. The player already has cards in the graveyard including Fatal Push copies, so having a fetch land available on the battlefield to crack at instant speed for Revolt is more valuable than saving 1 life. With the opponent at 20 and the player at 11, the 1 life matters somewhat, but the tactical flexibility of a fetch land on board outweighs this.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to play Plains as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Flooded Strand instead of Plains, keeping it available to crack for Revolt triggers or instant-speed deck interaction. The Plains could be played on a future turn when flexibility matters less.

annotations.description: Casting Emperor of Bones in the precombat main phase when the opponent has 3 open mana (Plains, Arena of Glory, Sacred Foundry) that could represent removal or interaction. The opponent's graveyard contains Galvanic Discharge, and they play a Boros deck that likely has removal. Additionally, Emperor of Bones's combat trigger won't exile anything useful from the opponent's graveyard this turn since it triggers at the beginning of combat - though it could target Phlage to prevent escape, which is actually valuable. However, playing a 2/2 into an opponent who could have Thraben Charm or other removal with no immediate value (the adapt costs additional mana) is somewhat risky. The alternative of holding up Flooded Strand + passing to represent interaction or waiting could be considered, though Emperor of Bones exiling Phlage from the opponent's graveyard at beginning of combat is genuinely important to prevent the escape threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Emperor of Bones in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Playing Flooded Strand first before casting Emperor of Bones would have been slightly better sequencing - it enables revolt for Fatal Push if needed later and thins the deck. The Emperor of Bones cast itself is reasonable given the need to exile Phlage from opponent's graveyard before they can escape it.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones likely has a creature exiled with it from the beginning of combat trigger (probably Orcish Bowmasters from own graveyard). With 1B available from untapped Godless Shrine and Plains, adapting Emperor of Bones in response to Thraben Charm would make it a 4/4 and reanimate the exiled creature with haste. This is significant value being left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emperor of Bones' adapt ability
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' adapt for 1B (using Plains and Godless Shrine) in response to Thraben Charm, growing Emperor to 4/4 and reanimating the exiled creature (likely Orcish Bowmasters) with haste for additional combat damage and board presence

annotations.description: With Thraben Charm on the stack (likely exiling graveyards), the player had exactly {1}{B} available (Plains + untapped Godless Shrine) to activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2. If the beginning of combat trigger already exiled a creature card from a graveyard, adapting would place +1/+1 counters on Emperor, triggering its reanimation ability to put that creature onto the battlefield with haste. Even if the graveyard exile mode was chosen, adapting in response preserves value. Additionally, the player skipped attacking entirely with Emperor of Bones (a 2/2) into an empty board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without adapting Emperor of Bones and then skipped the attack step entirely against an opponent with no creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B} using Plains and untapped Godless Shrine, potentially reanimating Orcish Bowmasters from exile. Then attack with Emperor of Bones into the empty board for damage.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones likely exiled Phlage from the opponent's graveyard at the beginning of combat. Activating Adapt 2 for {1}{B} would put +1/+1 counters on Emperor, triggering its ability to reanimate Phlage with haste. Phlage's ETB deals 3 damage and gains 3 life, and it would attack as a 6/6 this turn. The player had the mana available (Godless Shrine + Plains untapped). Even if Phlage wasn't exiled, other creatures like Ocelot Pride or Orcish Bowmasters could have been exiled and reanimated.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emperor of Bones' Adapt ability, missing the chance to reanimate a creature exiled with it.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 for {1}{B} to put +1/+1 counters on it, triggering the reanimation of the exiled creature (likely Phlage), getting a 6/6 hasty attacker plus 3 damage and 3 life from Phlage's ETB trigger.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones has an Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B}, and the player has 2 untapped lands (Godless Shrine and Plains) available to pay for it. Adapting would put +1/+1 counters on Emperor of Bones, making it a 4/4, and trigger its ability to put a creature card exiled with it onto the battlefield with haste. Even if no creature is currently exiled with it (the beginning of combat trigger may have exiled something), making Emperor a 4/4 is pure upside with no downside. The player has mana available and nothing else to spend it on, so declining to use this mana sink wastes resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emperor of Bones' Adapt ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B} using the untapped Godless Shrine and Plains, growing it to a 4/4 and potentially reanimating an exiled creature.

annotations.description: Gem25F Valley has Flooded Strand in hand and should play it as their land drop during precombat main phase. Missing land drops when you have lands available is always suboptimal, especially when it could provide additional mana for adapt activation or future plays. The reasoning also incorrectly states it's MiMo Sarge's turn when it's actually Gem25F Valley's turn 5.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing Flooded Strand from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Flooded Strand first (potentially crack it for a land to have more mana available), then proceed to combat for Emperor of Bones trigger, then activate Adapt to reanimate the exiled creature.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones could have been adapted for {1}{B} during combat using the two untapped lands (Godless Shrine + Plains). This would make it a 4/4 attacker and potentially reanimate a creature exiled with its beginning-of-combat trigger (likely Ocelot Pride from opponent's graveyard), giving it haste for additional combat damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emperor of Bones' adapt ability during their own combat step.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 for {1}{B} to make it 4/4 and trigger its reanimation ability, potentially putting a creature onto the battlefield with haste for additional combat damage.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones likely exiled a creature from a graveyard at the beginning of combat this turn. Activating Adapt 2 for {1}{B} during combat would make Emperor of Bones a 4/4 AND trigger its ability to put the exiled creature onto the battlefield with haste, giving an additional attacker. The player had plenty of mana available (4 lands untapped) and declined this significant combat advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emperor of Bones' Adapt ability during their own combat phase.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B} to make it a 4/4 and reanimate the exiled creature (likely Ocelot Pride or another creature from opponent's graveyard) with haste for an additional attacker.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones is a high-value engine piece that can reanimate creatures from graveyards (Phlage, Ocelot Pride, Orcish Bowmasters are all valid targets). Attacking it into a Seasoned Pyromancer that can profitably trade risks losing this engine for just 2 damage against 20 life. The opponent has incentive to block since Seasoned Pyromancer already got its ETB value.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Emperor of Bones into a board where Seasoned Pyromancer could trade.
annotations.betterLine: Hold back Emperor of Bones to use its exile and adapt/reanimate abilities over future turns, generating card advantage from the stocked graveyards.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 for {1}{B} during combat would make it a 4/4 attacker and trigger its reanimation ability to put any creature exiled with it onto the battlefield with haste. With 4 mana available and Emperor already attacking, this is significant free value - a bigger attacker plus potentially a free creature for the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emperor of Bones' Adapt ability, leaving 4 mana unused during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B} to make it a 4/4 and trigger the reanimation of any exiled creature, getting extra damage and board presence.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones (2/2) was attacking into Seasoned Pyromancer (2/2) and they traded. Adapting Emperor of Bones for {1}{B} would have made it a 4/4, letting it survive combat, kill Seasoned Pyromancer, and potentially trigger the +1/+1 counter ability to reanimate an exiled creature with haste. The mana was available (untapped Godless Shrines, Swamp, Plains).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Adapt, allowing Emperor of Bones to trade with Seasoned Pyromancer.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 for {1}{B} to make it a 4/4, survive combat, kill Seasoned Pyromancer, and trigger the reanimation ability from the +1/+1 counters.

annotations.description: MiMo Sarge could have escaped Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury this turn using Mountain (R to pay Arena's exert cost), Arena of Glory exerted (RR), Sacred Foundry (W), Plains (W) for exactly RRWW, exiling 5 of the 8 graveyard cards. This would put a 6/6 on the board, deal 3 damage to the opponent (putting them to 7), and gain 3 life. Instead they played Sacred Foundry and passed up deploying the most impactful threat available against an opponent at 10 life with an empty board.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Sacred Foundry (paying 2 life) instead of casting Phlage from graveyard.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury via escape (RRWW, exile 5 graveyard cards) to deploy a 6/6, deal 3 damage to opponent, and gain 3 life. Could still play a land afterward if desired.

annotations.description: MiMo Sarge has exactly enough mana (RRWW from 5 lands) and enough cards in graveyard (7 other cards, need 5) to escape Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury. The opponent is at 10 life with no creatures on board. Phlage would enter as a 6/6, deal 3 damage (opponent to 7), gain 3 life, and threaten another 3 damage on attack next turn. This is a game-dominating play that was completely passed on.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast either Seasoned Pyromancer or Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury from the graveyard.
annotations.betterLine: Escape Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury by paying RRWW and exiling 5 cards from graveyard. This puts a 6/6 on an empty board, deals 3 to opponent (bringing them to 7), and gains 3 life - likely winning the game in short order.

annotations.description: Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury can be escaped here for {R}{R}{W}{W} exiling 5 cards from the 7 available in graveyard. It creates a 6/6 body, deals 3 damage to the opponent (putting them to 7), and gains 3 life. This is vastly superior to Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability which only creates two 1/1 tokens. Phlage threatens lethal next attack (6 combat + 3 trigger = 9 vs opponent's 10, nearly lethal) and applies enormous pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to activate Seasoned Pyromancer from graveyard to create two 1/1 Elemental tokens
annotations.betterLine: Escape Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury to create a 6/6 threat that deals 3 damage and gains 3 life on entry, putting massive pressure on the opponent at 10 life

annotations.description: With the opponent at 7 life, Phlage escape was available (RRWW + exile 5 cards from 8-card graveyard) for a 6/6 that deals 3 damage on entry (putting opponent to 4) and gains 3 life. Playing Elegant Parlor (tapped land) as the first action is suboptimal sequencing - if they plan to cast Phlage this turn, they should lead with Phlage to avoid revealing information. If they don't cast Phlage at all, it's a much bigger mistake. Additionally, Arid Mesa would have been a better land drop as it can fetch an untapped land.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Elegant Parlor (enters tapped) as their first action
annotations.betterLine: Cast Phlage via escape immediately (RRWW from Mountain + Arena of Glory + 2x Sacred Foundry, exiling 5 graveyard cards) to deal 3 damage to opponent (putting them to 4 life) and deploy a 6/6 threat, then play a land.

annotations.description: At 7 life, played Watery Grave paying 2 life (going to 5) before casting Thoughtseize. They already have B mana available from Swamp/Godless Shrine to cast Thoughtseize this turn. Should cast Thoughtseize first to see opponent's hand and gather information before committing to a land drop. Additionally, paying 2 life for Watery Grave to enter untapped is likely unnecessary since they already have 6 lands with all colors available - it could safely enter tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Watery Grave paying 2 life (untapped) before casting any spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thoughtseize first using existing B mana to see opponent's hand, then play Watery Grave tapped (saving 2 life at a precarious 7 life total)

annotations.description: At 5 life, casting Thoughtseize loses 2 life going to 3, which puts them in range of Phlage's escape (3 damage ETB) that the opponent has available with 9 cards in graveyard and sufficient mana. The life loss is very dangerous in this position.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thoughtseize, going from 5 to 3 life
annotations.betterLine: Hardcast Solitude (3WW) to deploy a 3/2 lifelink creature that can block and gain life, helping stabilize at the critically low 5 life total. Solitude's lifelink is far more valuable than the disruption from Thoughtseize when the self-damage puts you in lethal range of Phlage escape.

annotations.description: At 5 life with Phlage in opponent's graveyard (which deals exactly 3 on ETB), paying 2 life for Thoughtseize drops to 3 life - exactly in Phlage escape lethal range. The opponent has enough mana colors (2x Sacred Foundry, Mountain, Arena of Glory, Plains) and 9 cards in graveyard (needs 5 to exile) to potentially escape Phlage next turn for exactly lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thoughtseize, going from 5 to 3 life
annotations.betterLine: Cast Solitude as a 3/2 lifelink creature (have 7 lands including white sources for 3WW). The lifelink body provides both a clock and life buffer. Even without a creature to exile with ETB, a 3/2 lifelink is critical when at 5 life facing potential Phlage escape.

annotations.description: Casting Thoughtseize at 5 life drops Gem25F Valley to 3 life, which puts them in lethal range of Phlage's escape (3 damage ETB trigger). The opponent has Phlage in graveyard with 9 cards available to exile 5, and enough mana ({R}{R}{W}{W}) across their lands. At 5 life, Phlage's 3 damage is survivable; at 3 life it's lethal. The only nonland card taken (Voice of Victory, a 1/3) is not worth the risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thoughtseize at 5 life, taking Voice of Victory and dropping to 3 life
annotations.betterLine: Don't cast Thoughtseize. Hold Solitude and Fatal Push as interaction, stay at 5 life to survive Phlage's ETB trigger if it escapes. Voice of Victory (1/3 with mobilize) is not threatening enough to justify the 2 life cost in this position.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life and Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury can be escaped from the graveyard for {R}{R}{W}{W} + exile 5 cards. MiMo Sarge has 9 cards in graveyard (enough to exile 5) and the mana to pay {R}{R}{W}{W} (Mountain, Arena of Glory for {R}{R}, Plains and Sacred Foundry/Elegant Parlor for {W}{W}). Phlage's ETB deals 3 damage to any target, which is exactly lethal against the opponent at 3 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Voice of Victory for 2 mana instead of escaping Phlage for the kill.
annotations.betterLine: Escape Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury from the graveyard, targeting the opponent with the 3 damage ETB trigger for lethal.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life. MiMo Sarge has Phlage in the graveyard with escape cost {R}{R}{W}{W} + exile 5 cards (9 other cards available in graveyard). With Sacred Foundry entering untapped (pay 2 life), the 4 untapped lands (Arena of Glory, existing Sacred Foundry, existing Elegant Parlor, new Sacred Foundry) would produce exactly {R}{R}{W}{W} to escape Phlage. Phlage's ETB deals 3 damage to any target, which is exactly lethal against the opponent at 3 life. Instead, Elegant Parlor enters tapped, leaving only 3 untapped lands and making Phlage uncastable this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Elegant Parlor (enters tapped) off Arid Mesa
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Sacred Foundry (pay 2 life, enters untapped), then escape Phlage for {R}{R}{W}{W} exiling 5 graveyard cards, dealing 3 damage to opponent at 3 life for lethal

annotations.description: At 3 life facing lethal on board (Voice of Victory + Ragavan = 5+ damage next attack), spending 1 life to fetch a land with 8 lands already in play is wasteful. Voice of Victory is MV 2, so Fatal Push already kills it without needing revolt. The life point matters significantly at 3 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Flooded Strand to fetch a land, paying 1 life to go to 2 life with 8 lands already on board.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fatal Push targeting Voice of Victory immediately (MV 2, no revolt needed), preserving the life point and eliminating the most dangerous threat that also locks out spells during opponent's turn. Then hardcast Solitude next turn to exile Ragavan and gain a lifelink blocker.

annotations.description: At 3 life facing Ragavan (2/1) and Voice of Victory (1/3 with Mobilize 2), only removing one threat leaves the player still facing lethal or near-lethal damage next turn. Both creatures need to be addressed this turn since Voice of Victory prevents casting during opponent's turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Likely cast only Fatal Push, leaving Ragavan on board while at 3 life
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fatal Push targeting Voice of Victory AND hard-cast Solitude (5 mana available from 8 lands) targeting Ragavan to completely clear the board and survive. Solitude's lifelink body also provides a blocker and life buffer.

annotations.description: Gem25F Valley is at 3 life facing lethal next turn from Ragavan (2/1) + Voice of Victory (1/3 with Mobilize 2 creating two 1/1 attackers) = 5 damage. Voice of Victory also prevents casting spells during opponent's turn, so they can't Fatal Push during MiMo's combat. They have the mana to hard-cast Solitude (3WW with 7+ untapped lands) to exile Voice of Victory, which would remove the spell-lock, the mobilize tokens, and leave Solitude as a 3/2 lifelink blocker against Ragavan.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything, leaving lethal attackers on board with no ability to interact during opponent's turn due to Voice of Victory's spell-lock.
annotations.betterLine: Hard-cast Solitude (3WW) targeting Voice of Victory to exile it, removing the combat lock and lethal threat. Solitude's 3/2 lifelink body can then block Ragavan, and Fatal Push remains available for future use.

annotations.description: Voice of Victory prevents opponents from casting spells during MiMo Sarge's turn. At 3 life, Gem25F Valley faces lethal from Ragavan (2/1) + Voice of Victory (1/3) + two Mobilize warrior tokens. By passing without removing Voice of Victory or Ragavan, Gem25F Valley will be completely locked out of casting Solitude or Fatal Push during MiMo Sarge's next combat, making lethal unavoidable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spells during their own combat step.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Solitude (evoking by exiling Fatal Push) to exile Voice of Victory, removing both the spell-lock and a significant attacker. Alternatively, at minimum cast Fatal Push on Ragavan to reduce incoming damage, since these spells cannot be cast during the opponent's turn while Voice of Victory is in play.

annotations.description: Voice of Victory prevents casting spells during opponent's turn, and the opponent has lethal on board next attack (Voice of Victory 1 + Mobilize 2 warriors + Ragavan 2 = 5 damage vs 3 life). By passing without removing threats, Gem25F Valley will die next turn with no ability to interact.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spells, holding Fatal Push and Solitude for a 'better moment'
annotations.betterLine: Hard-cast Solitude (3WW, which is available from 8 lands including multiple white sources) targeting Voice of Victory to exile it, removing both the lethal Mobilize threat and the 'can't cast spells during opponent's turn' restriction. Alternatively, Fatal Push Voice of Victory (MV 2) to at least reduce incoming damage significantly.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life and MiMo Sarge has no cards in hand except a land. Activating Seasoned Pyromancer from the graveyard for {3}{R}{R} would create two 1/1 Elemental tokens, providing additional attackers to close out the game next turn against an opponent at 3 life. With 6 untapped lands and nothing else to spend mana on, there's no reason not to activate this.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability ({3}{R}{R}) to create two 1/1 Elemental tokens, increasing board pressure against an opponent at 3 life.
